# What Is DataVo?

> Source route: /manual/preface/what-is-datavo
> Source file: manual/preface/what-is-datavo.md

DataVo is an embedded database engine for .NET applications. You add it to a process, create a `DataVoContext`, and run SQL against local storage. There is no separate database service to deploy for the core engine.

The simplest mental model is SQLite-style deployment with a C#-native implementation. DataVo is not trying to look like PostgreSQL in v0.2 Release Candidate (`v0.2.0-rc.3`). It is designed to make local storage fast and ergonomic for .NET 10 workloads that benefit from in-process execution, allocation-aware hot paths, vector search, and locked Native AOT compatibility.

The smallest DataVo program creates an in-memory database, defines a table, inserts a row, and reads it back.

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory
});

db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Demo");
db.Execute("USE Demo");

db.Execute("""
CREATE TABLE Users (
  Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  Name VARCHAR(80)
);
""");

db.Execute("INSERT INTO Users (Id, Name) VALUES (1, 'Ada')");

var result = db.Execute("SELECT Id, Name FROM Users WHERE Id = 1")[0];
Console.WriteLine(result.Data[0]["Name"]);
```

For persisted data, the same API switches to disk-backed storage. The high-throughput path is `StorageMode.Lsm`, which uses WAL-covered MemTables and SSTables.

```csharp
using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./datavo_lsm_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true
});
```

DataVo also has SQL support for vector columns. That makes it possible to keep application records and embeddings in the same embedded engine.

```sql
CREATE TABLE Documents (
  Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  Title VARCHAR(200),
  Embedding VECTOR(1536)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_documents_embedding
ON Documents (Embedding)
USING HNSW;
```

DataVo v0.2 Release Candidate (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) is built for local-first .NET 10 applications, game tooling, simulations, vector-search workloads, and high-throughput embedded persistence. It should not be presented as a client/server RDBMS or a PostgreSQL-compatible server.

## v0.2 Positioning

In v0.2 (`v0.2.0-rc.3`), DataVo provides an embedded C# storage engine (`DataVoContext` and `DataVoConnection` running in-process), `InMemory` and `Lsm` storage (`Disk` paged mode is legacy), its own compact SQL dialect for DDL/DML/queries, zero-allocation in-memory point lookups (`56 B`, ~`405 ns`), and SIMD vector columns and indexes (`VECTOR(n)`, `USING HNSW`, `USING FLAT`, `<=>`, `<->`). Native AOT (`DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Data`) is locked with trim and AOT analyzers enforced as build errors. DataVo is deliberately **not** a full client/server RDBMS — it is not PostgreSQL, SQLite, or SQL Server wire-compatible — and its client/server tooling bridge (`DataVo.Server`) is planned for the v0.3+ roadmap. See the [SQL compatibility matrix](/manual/sql-language/sql-compatibility) for the authoritative feature status.

---

# Project Status & Stability

> Source route: /manual/preface/project-status
> Source file: manual/preface/project-status.md

**Current release: v0.2.0-rc.3 (Release Candidate).**

DataVo is a C#-native embedded database engine. The 0.2 line is feature-complete for its documented scope and is in release verification: benchmark runs, crash-recovery testing and package publishing checks are ongoing before a stable tag. This page is the single place that states what that means in practice.

## What "Release Candidate" means here

- The documented API surface and SQL dialect are the surface being verified for 0.2. Changes to it between release candidates are called out in the release notes.
- Behavior outside the documented surface is not covered by that expectation. [Limits](/manual/reference/limits) and [Unsupported Features](/manual/reference/unsupported-features) list those boundaries.
- Release candidates are published to nuget.org as prerelease packages. Add `--prerelease` when installing. See [Installation & Packages](/manual/getting-started/installation).
- The on-disk storage format is not yet covered by a long-term compatibility guarantee. Keep a way to rebuild important data (an export, seed data or an import script) until a stable release states one.

## Subsystem status

| Subsystem | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Embedded API (`DataVoContext`) | Release candidate | The primary interface. |
| SQL dialect (DDL, DML, queries) | Release candidate | DataVo's own dialect, not PostgreSQL-compatible. See the [compatibility matrix](/manual/sql-language/sql-compatibility). |
| In-Memory storage | Release candidate | Ephemeral by design. |
| LSM-Tree storage | Release candidate | The recommended persistent engine: WAL, MemTable, SSTables, strict fsync by default. |
| Disk storage (paged) | Legacy | Kept for existing data. It receives no further durability work. Prefer LSM. |
| Transactions and MVCC | Release candidate | No serializable guarantee for arbitrary multi-row predicates. See [Transactions](/manual/storage-engine/transactions-acid-mvcc). |
| Compiled LINQ and source generators | Release candidate | Supported shapes are listed in [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators). Other shapes fall back to the interpreter. |
| Vector search (HNSW and FLAT) | Release candidate | Cosine and L2 distance. See [Vector Search Syntax](/manual/sql-language/vector-search-syntax). |
| ADO.NET provider (`DataVo.Data`) | Release candidate | Standard `System.Data.Common` types. See [ADO.NET Provider](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net). |
| Dapper | Works through ADO.NET | No separate package. See [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper). |
| Entity Framework Core integration | Bridge | Attaches DataVo to an EF context with a host EF provider. It is not a standalone provider and has no migrations. See [Entity Framework Core](/manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework). |
| Native AOT | Supported | `DataVo.Core` and `DataVo.Data` build with the trim and AOT analyzers as errors. |
| Browser / WebAssembly (`DataVo.Browser`) | Experimental / Playground Lane | Interactive documentation playground (`docs/src/DataVoClient.ts`); not a production target and not published on npm. |
| PostgreSQL replication (DataVo-Sync) | Separate product | Not part of the NuGet packages. Proprietary replication bridge to PostgreSQL. |
| Unity | Evaluation target | See below. |

## Preview contracts

SQL `DATE` materializes as `DataVo.Core.DataVoDate` in the row APIs. `CellValue.AsDate()` and compiled `GetDate` return `DataVoDate`; modern .NET callers keep explicit `FromDateOnly`, `ToDateOnly`, `AsDateOnly` and `GetDateOnly` adapters. Existing persisted `DATE` bytes are unchanged.

## Unity Evaluation Status

Unity is an evaluation target, not a supported runtime. The public `DataVo.Core` package contains only a `net10.0` asset. `DataVoEnablePortableTarget=true` creates an experimental local `netstandard2.1` candidate only. A passing .NET-host verifier by itself is not Unity Editor, Mono, IL2CPP, Jobs, or Burst proof.

| Environment or boundary | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unity 6000.5.4f1 Editor | Verified (narrow smoke) | The tracked project imports the generated candidate and its EditMode smoke suite passes. |
| macOS IL2CPP (6000.5.4f1) | Verified (narrow smoke) | A Medium-stripping Player builds, launches, performs the Unity type-binding scenario, writes a passing report, and exits zero. |
| Windows x64 IL2CPP | Unverified | Windows requires its own built-and-executed Player proof. |
| Direct Burst calls | Unsupported by design | DataVo uses managed engine types and services and is not a Burst job payload. |
| Job-to-managed batch bridge | Planned proof | A Burst-compatible job may produce POD commands that managed code drains after completion. |
| In-memory mode | Candidate scope | This is the only storage mode included in the Stage 3 Unity candidate proof. |
| Disk/LSM persistence | Verified (narrow smoke) | Save, close and reopen pass for both modes in the Unity 6000.5.4f1 macOS Editor and a macOS IL2CPP Player. Other platforms and power-loss behaviour are unverified. |

## Scope summary

| Feature | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In-process embedded deployment | Supported | The core product shape is library-first, not server-first. |
| Public curated manual | Supported | The manual is the public documentation boundary. |
| SQL execution through `DataVoContext` | Supported | Core SQL commands and query forms are documented. |
| ADO.NET provider | Supported | `DataVoConnection`, `DataVoCommand`, `DataVoDataReader`; Dapper works through it. |
| Entity Framework bridge | Supported | Basic `DbSet` workflows and query previews with explicit operator limits, not a full provider. |
| Roslyn source generators | Supported | `[DataVoQuery]` and typed table queries compile at build time. |
| NuGet packaging | Supported | Four packages. The public Core package is `net10.0`-only; the opt-in portable target is an experimental local candidate, not a published or supported Unity asset. |
| Stable storage format | Planned | Requires compatibility tests and migration guidance. |
| Production support contract | Not Supported | No production support contract is offered. |
| Stored procedures, triggers, PostgreSQL-compatible server | Not Supported | See [Unsupported Features](/manual/reference/unsupported-features). |

# Release Scope & Boundaries (v0.2 Release Candidate)

> Source route: /manual/preface/alpha-scope
> Source file: manual/preface/alpha-scope.md

DataVo v0.2 Release Candidate (v0.2.0-rc.3) defines the feature-complete verification boundary for the 0.2 release line, backed by 2,358 passing tests across the engine, storage, and client suites. It establishes a clear contract between release-candidate core subsystems and explicit engine boundaries.

The supported path starts with direct embedding. Create a context, choose a storage mode, and execute SQL or typed queries from your .NET 10 application. In-memory mode includes a zero-allocation primary-key point lookup fast path (`56 B` ADO.NET reader wrapper, ~`405 ns`).

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory
});

db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE RcDemo");
db.Execute("USE RcDemo");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE Events (Id INT PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(80))");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO Events (Id, Name) VALUES (1, 'created')");
```

For persisted workloads, `StorageMode.Lsm` with `LsmStrictFsync = true` is the release-candidate storage engine, using WAL-backed MemTables, SSTables, and clustered primary keys so acknowledged writes wait for WAL durability. Disk paged mode (`StorageMode.Disk`) is legacy and receives no further durability work. See [WAL And Durability](../storage-engine/wal-and-durability.md#known-limitations) for durability notes and legacy disk mode limitations.

```csharp
using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./rc_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true
});
```

The SQL surface is documented as a verified subset. You can create tables, insert rows, update rows, delete rows, query rows, build scalar and vector indexes, and run SIMD-accelerated vector search (`HNSW` and `FLAT` with cosine `<=>` and L2 `<->` distance). Native AOT (`DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Data`) is locked with trim and AOT analyzers enforced as build errors.

```sql
CREATE TABLE Products (
  Id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  Name VARCHAR(120),
  Price FLOAT,
  Embedding VECTOR(3)
);

INSERT INTO Products (Id, Name, Price, Embedding)
VALUES (1, 'Example', 12.5, '[1,0,0]');

SELECT Id, Name
FROM Products
WHERE Price > 10
ORDER BY Price DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

## Explicit Boundaries

DataVo v0.2 Release Candidate (v0.2.0-rc.3) enforces strict architectural boundaries so adopters can evaluate the engine with accurate expectations:

- **No arbitrary multi-row serializable MVCC:** Transactions provide session-bound `BEGIN TRANSACTION` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`, row-level write coordination, and MVCC snapshot visibility, but do not guarantee serializable isolation or phantom-read prevention across arbitrary multi-row predicates.
- **EF Core migrations unsupported:** `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` operates as an integration bridge over a host EF provider for bounded `DbSet` and `QueryFromDataVo` workflows, not a standalone EF Core provider with migration scaffolding.
- **Disk paged mode is legacy:** `StorageMode.Disk` is retained only for compatibility and receives no further durability engineering. All persistent workloads should use `StorageMode.Lsm`.
- **WebAssembly is an experimental playground lane:** `DataVo.Browser` powers the interactive documentation playground (`docs/src/DataVoClient.ts`), but is **not** a production-ready target and is **not** published on npm.

## Preview SQL DATE Contract

SQL `DATE` now materializes as `DataVo.Core.DataVoDate` in preview row APIs. `CellValue.AsDate()` and compiled `GetDate` return `DataVoDate`; modern .NET callers retain explicit `FromDateOnly`, `ToDateOnly`, `AsDateOnly`, and `GetDateOnly` adapters. Existing persisted `DATE` bytes are unchanged.

## Unity Evaluation Status

Unity is an evaluation target, not a supported runtime in DataVo v0.2 Release Candidate (v0.2.0-rc.3). The public `DataVo.Core` package contains only a `net10.0` asset. `DataVoEnablePortableTarget=true` creates an experimental local `netstandard2.1` candidate only. A passing .NET-host verifier by itself is not Unity Editor, Mono, IL2CPP, Jobs, or Burst proof.

| Environment or boundary | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unity 6000.5.4f1 Editor | Verified (narrow smoke) | The tracked project imports the generated candidate and its EditMode smoke suite passes. |
| macOS IL2CPP (6000.5.4f1) | Verified (narrow smoke) | A Medium-stripping Player builds, launches, performs the Unity type-binding scenario, writes a passing report, and exits zero. |
| Windows x64 IL2CPP | Unverified | Windows requires its own built-and-executed Player proof. |
| Direct Burst calls | Unsupported by design | DataVo uses managed engine types and services and is not a Burst job payload. |
| Job-to-managed batch bridge | Planned proof | A Burst-compatible job may produce POD commands that managed code drains after completion. |
| In-memory mode | Candidate scope | This is the only storage mode included in the Stage 3 Unity candidate proof. |
| Disk/LSM persistence | Verified (narrow smoke) | Save, close and reopen pass for both modes in the Unity 6000.5.4f1 macOS Editor and a macOS IL2CPP Player. Other platforms and power-loss behaviour are unverified. |

## v0.2 Release Candidate Scope Summary

| Feature | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core embedded API (`DataVoContext`) | Release Candidate | Primary in-process embedded interface (`net10.0`). |
| LSM storage with strict fsync | Release Candidate | WAL-backed MemTables, SSTables, and clustered primary keys (`LsmStrictFsync = true`). |
| Zero-alloc in-memory point lookup | Release Candidate | Direct PK fast path (`56 B` reader allocation, ~`405 ns` lookup). |
| SIMD vector search (`HNSW` & `FLAT`) | Release Candidate | `VECTOR(n)` columns with cosine (`<=>`) and Euclidean/L2 (`<->`) operators. |
| Native AOT (`DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Data`) | Locked & Passing | Trim and AOT analyzers (`IL2026`/`IL3050`) enforced as build errors. |
| ADO.NET & Dapper (`DataVo.Data`) | Release Candidate | Standard `DbConnection`, `DbCommand`, `DbDataReader` provider surface. |
| Roslyn source generators (`DataVo.Generators`) | Release Candidate | `[DataVoQuery]` compiled query plans and typed row mappers. |
| Entity Framework Core bridge | Preview Bridge | Supports bounded `DbSet` and `QueryFromDataVo` workflows; EF migrations are unsupported. |
| Disk paged storage (`StorageMode.Disk`) | Legacy | Retained for compatibility; receives no further durability work. |
| Browser / WebAssembly (`DataVo.Browser`) | Experimental / Playground Lane | Powers the interactive docs playground; not a production target and not published on npm. |
| Arbitrary multi-row serializable MVCC | Not Supported | Snapshot visibility and row-level write locks only; no predicate-range locking. |
| Full RDBMS server features | Not Supported | No stored procedures, triggers, replication, or PostgreSQL wire server in v0.2. |

# Roadmap

> Source route: /manual/preface/roadmap
> Source file: manual/preface/roadmap.md

DataVo's roadmap separates completed **v0.2 Release Candidate (`v0.2.0-rc.3`)** milestones from active **v0.3 HTAP & Tooling** engineering. The core design principle remains unchanged: predictable in-process storage, explicit durability contracts, locked Native AOT compliance, and allocation-aware execution paths.

```csharp
using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig
{
    StorageMode = StorageMode.Lsm,
    DiskStoragePath = "./app_data",
    LsmStrictFsync = true
});
```

## Completed v0.2 Milestones (`v0.2.0-rc.3`)

The v0.2 release line has completed its foundational embedded engine milestones and is backed by 2,358 passing tests:

- **LSM Storage Stability & Clustered Keys:** WAL-backed arena MemTables, background SSTable flushes, strict `fsync` durability (`LsmStrictFsync = true`), and clustered `INT`/`GUID` primary keys that halve on-disk footprint.
- **Locked Native AOT:** `DataVo.Core` and `DataVo.Data` enforce trim and AOT analyzers (`IL2026`/`IL3050`) as build errors.
- **Zero-Allocation In-Memory Fast Path:** Primary-key point lookups bypass SQL parsing and dictionary materialization (`56 B` ADO.NET reader wrapper, ~`405 ns`), alongside zero-allocation `StreamRef()` / `RowRef` table scans.
- **SIMD Vector Search:** Built-in `VECTOR(n)` columns (`VEC2`, `VEC3`, `VEC4` shorthands), `HNSW` and `FLAT` indexes, and SIMD-accelerated cosine (`<=>`) and Euclidean/L2 (`<->`) distance operators.
- **NuGet Release Candidate Packaging:** `DataVo.Core`, `DataVo.Data`, `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore`, and `DataVo.Generators` are published to nuget.org via CI Trusted Publishing (`--prerelease`).

```bash
dotnet add package DataVo.Core --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.Data --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.Generators --prerelease
```

## Active v0.3 Roadmap: HTAP, Compact Rows & Wire Tooling

Active engineering for **v0.3** focuses on closing the analytical scan gap with columnar engines while preserving DataVo's sub-microsecond OLTP point lookups:

### 1. Columnar Indexes for HTAP (Hybrid Transactional/Analytical Processing)

While DataVo v0.2 leads SQLite on compiled in-memory aggregates and OLTP point lookups, full analytical table scans over 1M+ rows remain faster on pure column stores like DuckDB. In v0.3, DataVo is introducing **Columnar Indexes** so tables can maintain synchronized columnar projections alongside row storage, enabling SIMD-vectorized analytical scans, filtered aggregations, and `GROUP BY` pipelines directly on contiguous column buffers.

### 2. Compact In-Memory Row Layout

v0.3 overhauls the in-memory row representation into a dense, contiguous layout that eliminates per-row object header overhead, reduces memory footprint on multi-million-row tables, and improves CPU cache-line utilization during scans and index probes.

### 3. PostgreSQL-Wire Tooling Bridge (`DataVo.Server`)

Developers need to inspect embedded DataVo databases from standard GUI clients such as DBeaver, DataGrip, and pgAdmin. `DataVo.Server` is planned as an optional companion host implementing a subset of the PostgreSQL wire protocol and catalog views (`pg_catalog`) over an existing DataVo storage directory.

```text
Application process (OLTP + HTAP)
  -> DataVoContext / DataVoConnection
  -> Row store + v0.3 Columnar Indexes
  -> Embedded LSM / In-Memory storage

Future tooling process (v0.3+)
  -> DataVo.Server
  -> PostgreSQL wire protocol subset
  -> Embedded LSM storage
```

## Planned v0.4

### On-Disk Columnar SSTable Storage (Out-of-core Parquet-style chunks)

In v0.3 a columnar index on an LSM table is derived state held in memory: it is rebuilt from the table's rows on first use after the database is opened, and it does not change how rows are stored, so primary-key lookups on the LSM engine keep their cost (239 ns in the current benchmarks). That design needs RAM for every indexed column, which rules it out for datasets larger than memory.

v0.4 plans native columnar storage in the SSTable format itself: column chunks written at flush and merged at compaction, read from disk a chunk at a time, so analytical scans work on data that does not fit in memory and nothing has to be rebuilt on open. This is planned work; nothing of it exists yet.

## Ecosystem & Platform Evaluation Lanes

- **Unity Integration (Evaluation Target):** A narrow managed, in-memory candidate has passed a pinned Unity 6000.5.4f1 Editor and macOS IL2CPP Player smoke. Direct Burst calls are unsupported by design; Windows IL2CPP validation and broader game-save durability proofs remain separate evaluation gates.
- **WebAssembly (`Experimental / Playground Lane`):** `DataVo.Browser` (`docs/src/DataVoClient.ts`) powers the interactive documentation playground, but is **not** a production target and is **not** published on npm.

## Roadmap Summary

| Milestone / Feature | Status | Target / Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core embedded API (`DataVoContext`) & ADO.NET (`DataVo.Data`) | Completed (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) | Primary in-process interfaces on .NET 10. |
| LSM storage stability & clustered PKs | Completed (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) | Strict WAL `fsync`, SSTables, and clustered `INT`/`GUID` keys. |
| Native AOT lock (`DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Data`) | Completed (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) | Trim and AOT analyzers enforced as build errors. |
| Zero-alloc in-memory point lookup & `RowRef` streaming | Completed (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) | `56 B`, ~`405 ns` PK fast path; 0 B heap allocation on `StreamRef()`. |
| SIMD vector search (`HNSW` & `FLAT`) | Completed (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) | Cosine (`<=>`) and L2 (`<->`) distance operators. |
| NuGet prerelease packages | Completed (`v0.2.0-rc.3`) | Published to nuget.org via CI Trusted Publishing. |
| Columnar Indexes for HTAP | Completed (`v0.3`) | Synchronized columnar buffers on In-Memory and LSM tables; beats DuckDB by up to 8.9× on covered aggregates. |
| Compact in-memory row layout | Completed (`v0.3`) | `FlatRowStore` + direct `PackedKeyReader<T>`: 13× lower row-store memory (`49.2 B/row`) and `52.1 ns` PK lookup. |
| On-disk columnar SSTable storage (out-of-core, Parquet-style chunks) | Planned (`v0.4`) | Analytical scans over datasets larger than memory, with no rebuild on open. |
| PostgreSQL-wire tooling bridge (`DataVo.Server`) | Planned (`v0.3+`) | Connect DBeaver, DataGrip, and pgAdmin to DataVo storage. |
| Long-term on-disk format stability guarantee | Planned | Requires cross-version compatibility suite and migration tooling. |
| Unity managed integration proof | Evaluation Target | Narrow Unity 6000.5.4f1 Editor and macOS IL2CPP smoke passed; Windows x64 unverified. |
| Browser / WebAssembly (`DataVo.Browser`) | `Experimental / Playground Lane` | Interactive docs playground only; not production-ready and not published on npm. |
| EF Core migrations | Not Supported | `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` is a query/DML bridge, not a migration provider. |
| Multi-node replication & high availability | Not Supported | Out of scope for the embedded engine. |

# Installation & Packages

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/installation
> Source file: manual/getting-started/installation.md

DataVo ships as four NuGet packages. Install only the ones you need: `DataVo.Core` is the engine and everything else builds on it.

The current release is **v0.2.0-rc.3 (Release Candidate)**, so include `--prerelease` when you add a package. See [Project Status & Stability](/manual/preface/project-status) for what that means.

## Packages

| Package | Install it when you want | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DataVo.Core` | The embedded engine and SQL through `DataVoContext`. | Parser, planner, storage engines (In-Memory, LSM-Tree, legacy Disk), vector indexes, typed table API. |
| `DataVo.Data` | An ADO.NET provider, or a micro-ORM such as Dapper. | `DataVoConnection`, `DataVoCommand`, `DataVoDataReader`, `DataVoTransaction`, `DataVoParameter`. |
| `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | An EF Core `DbContext` over DataVo. | `UseDataVo(...)`, `DataVoDbContext`, query-translation diagnostics. |
| `DataVo.Generators` | Compiled LINQ queries and `[DataVoQuery]` methods. | A Roslyn source generator and analyzer. It is a build-time reference, not a runtime dependency. |

```bash
dotnet add package DataVo.Core --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.Data --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore --prerelease
dotnet add package DataVo.Generators --prerelease
```

## Which packages for which job

| Job | Packages |
| --- | --- |
| Embedded SQL and the typed table API | `DataVo.Core` |
| Compiled LINQ scans and aggregates | `DataVo.Core` and `DataVo.Generators` |
| ADO.NET or Dapper | `DataVo.Data` (brings `DataVo.Core`) |
| EF Core | `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` (brings `DataVo.Core`) |

## Requirements

- **.NET 10.** The published `DataVo.Core` package contains a `net10.0` asset only. Other targets, including Unity, are not supported. See [Project Status](/manual/preface/project-status#unity-evaluation-status).
- **Native AOT** is supported by `DataVo.Core` and `DataVo.Data`. See [Native AOT Deployment](/manual/client-interfaces/native-aot).
- **C# interceptors** are used by `DataVo.Generators`. The package's build props register the `DataVo.Generated` interceptors namespace for you, so no manual `InterceptorsNamespaces` entry is needed.

## Verify the install

```csharp
using DataVo.Core;
using DataVo.Core.StorageEngine.Config;

using var db = new DataVoContext(new DataVoConfig { StorageMode = StorageMode.InMemory });
db.Execute("CREATE DATABASE Smoke");
db.Execute("USE Smoke");
db.Execute("CREATE TABLE T (Id INT PRIMARY KEY)");
db.Execute("INSERT INTO T (Id) VALUES (1)");

Console.WriteLine(db.Execute("SELECT Id FROM T")[0].Data.Count); // 1
```

Continue with the [Quickstart](/manual/tutorial/quickstart), or pick an API in [Choosing an Interface](/manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface). See also [Project Status & Scope](/manual/preface/project-status).

---

# Choosing an Interface

> Source route: /manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface
> Source file: manual/getting-started/choosing-an-interface.md

DataVo has five ways to talk to the same engine. They differ in ergonomics and in how much work happens per call, not in what the database can store. You can mix them in one application.

## Decision table

| Interface | Package | Best for | Per-call cost | Native AOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Compiled LINQ](/manual/client-interfaces/source-generators) | `DataVo.Core` + `DataVo.Generators` | Hot paths: point lookups, filtered counts and aggregates. | Lowest. Predicates are compiled at build time; aggregates allocate nothing once warm. | Yes |
| [Embedded API](/manual/client-interfaces/datavo-context-api) (`DataVoContext`) | `DataVo.Core` | Application code that wants SQL, DDL, vector search and full control. | Parses SQL per call unless prepared. Rows come back as dictionaries. | Yes |
| [ADO.NET provider](/manual/client-interfaces/ado-net) | `DataVo.Data` | Code or libraries that already speak `DbConnection`. | Same engine as the embedded API, behind the standard ADO.NET types. | Yes |
| [Dapper](/manual/client-interfaces/dapper) | `DataVo.Data` + `Dapper` | Micro-ORM mapping with plain SQL. | ADO.NET cost plus Dapper's mapping. | Per Dapper's own support |
| [Entity Framework Core](/manual/client-interfaces/entity-framework) | `DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore` | Existing EF models and `DbContext` workflows. | Highest. EF infrastructure sits on top of the engine. | Not claimed |

A short rule of thumb:

- Start with the **embedded API** to learn the engine and for anything that is not performance critical.
- Move the few queries that run constantly to **compiled LINQ**.
- Use **ADO.NET or Dapper** when you are adapting existing code or want a familiar abstraction.
- Use **EF Core** when the rest of your application is already modelled in EF.

## How they fit together

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  App["Your application"]
  App --> LINQ["Compiled LINQ<br/>(DataVo.Generators)"]
  App --> Ctx["DataVoContext<br/>(DataVo.Core)"]
  App --> Ado["ADO.NET provider<br/>(DataVo.Data)"]
  App --> EF["EF Core integration<br/>(DataVo.EntityFrameworkCore)"]
  Dapper["Dapper"] --> Ado
  LINQ --> Core["DataVo.Core engine"]
  Ctx --> Core
  Ado --> Core
  EF --> Core
  Core --> Storage["In-Memory | LSM-Tree | Disk (legacy)"]
```

Every route ends in the same parser, planner and storage engines, so storage modes, durability settings and vector indexes behave identically whichever interface you use.

## The same question, five ways

"How many players are level 10 or higher?" The table is `players (Id INT PRIMARY KEY, Level INT)`.

**Embedded API**

```csharp
var result = db.Execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total FROM players WHERE Level >= 10")[0];
object total = result.Data[0]["Total"];
```

**ADO.NET**

```csharp
using var cmd = connection.CreateCommand();
cmd.CommandText = "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players WHERE Level >= @min";
cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@min", 10);
object? total = cmd.ExecuteScalar();
```

**Dapper**

```csharp
int total = connection.ExecuteScalar<int>(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players WHERE Level >= @min", new { min = 10 });
```

**Entity Framework Core**

```csharp
List<Player> matches = context.QueryFromDataVo<Player>(query =>
    query.Where(static p => p.Level >= 10));
int total = matches.Count;
```

**Compiled LINQ**

```csharp
int total = db.Table<Player>().Where(10, static (p, min) => p.Level >= min).Count();
```

The compiled form reads the `Level` cell straight from the stored bytes and builds no `Player` objects. That is the mechanism behind the zero-allocation aggregates described in [Compiled Scan Kernels](/manual/internals/compiled-scan-kernels).

- [Installation & Packages](/manual/getting-started/installation)
- [ADO.NET & Dapper tutorial](/manual/tutorial/ado-net-and-dapper)
- [Benchmark Results](/manual/performance/benchmarks), to see what each approach costs in practice.
